events.prompt: One continuous, atmospheric winter photograph, taken from a single camera position at eye level, standing in a quiet hot-spring town lane at blue hour in gentle snowfall and looking along it with natural perspective. The lane runs away from the camera and bends gently to the left between old dark-timber inns with closed wooden lattice doors; their snow-laden eaves recede in one line under a deep-blue evening sky, and a few small plain paper lanterns glow beneath them, getting smaller into the distance. The same smooth, fresh snow covers the ground all the way from the foreground, where it is untouched, back along the lane. A 24-year-old adult Korean woman with honey-orange brown hair in a layered wolf cut, wearing a long deep-cranberry wool coat over an ivory knit mini dress and white knee-high boots, walks slowly along the lane with her hands in her coat pockets, glancing up at the falling snow with a soft smile, her face in three-quarter view. She is a modest figure a little right of centre, part of the street rather than in front of it; her whole body is visible, both boots stand on the snow, and open snow stretches between her and the camera. The nearest lantern lights her face, her coat and the snow around her with warm amber light; everything else stays cool blue. It is a quiet pedestrian lane: plain timber walls, lattice doors, lanterns and snow are all there is.
